name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after 20% gas cuts to plants; Gulf exports still disrupted by Hormuz restrictions
state: Egyptian granular urea rose to about $535 a tonne as gas supplies to fertiliser plants were cut by 20% from 1 Nov (EnterpriseAM, 4 Nov; UkrAgroConsult). Gulf fertiliser exports remain disrupted by Iran's Hormuz restrictions, with new mine strike claims on 15 Nov. Searches on 15 Nov found no 60% three-month rise in urea or a fully closed export route, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring are exposed to higher costs, which can feed into food prices next year.
rubric_hit: Watch: Gulf urea exports restricted and Egyptian supply curbed; no >60% three-month rise or closed route for Alert

sources.title: EnterpriseAM Egypt — Egyptian granular urea at USD 535 as gas supplies to fertilizer plants cut 20%
UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
